description: IDC deterministic-core hooks (v4). SessionEnd: the recirculation-intake safety-net sweep (re-stages rogue Buildables, captures untickered discovery/deferral markers). Stop: the fixpoint gate — an autorun/build orchestrator DRAIN session (self-gated via the ledger's session-scoped orchestrator_drain marker) cannot stop while `idc_autorun_drain.py` reports `drain: recirc-pending` (exit 4) AND the ledger agrees work remains; the ledger alone never blocks a clean board (drain: complete wins), bounded N=3 then loud-fail + a one-time board annotation. SubagentStop: (1) the verdict gate — a review agent cannot stop without a validated verdict JSON at docs/workflow/code-reviews/ (bounded N=3, then loud-fail); (2) the recirculator closeout-or-checkpoint detective — when the recirculator subagent stops mid-drain WITHOUT a valid idc_recirc_closeout.py closeout, every still-open Stage=Recirculation ∧ Status=Todo inbox ticket gets a resume-checkpoint comment {branch, PR#, dispositions} reconstructed deterministically from the agent transcript + a recirc_checkpoint:<ticket> ledger taint (drop F); a valid closeout allows + clears the taints. Post-hoc detective — fail-OPEN, never blocks the stop; records under observe-only. PreToolUse (Bash/Write/Edit/NotebookEdit): the shared Path Gate transport — raw `gh issue create` / `gh pr merge` / `gh issue close` / state-closing or dependency `gh api` (`dependencies/blocked_by` POST/DELETE) / raw board mutation (`gh project item-edit|item-add|item-delete`, GraphQL board/issue writes) that bypasses the transition engine / finisher tail, INCLUDING one hidden behind interpreter indirection (`bash|sh|zsh FILE`, `source`/`.` FILE, a quoted `bash -c` payload — resolved by bounded, cycle-guarded, sensitive-file-refusing inspection), OR a direct Write/Edit/NotebookEdit repository mutation without a live authorization, is evaluated by the shared core. WHAT THE FILE DOORS DO NOT GATE: the gate guards APPLICATION CODE, executable/security policy, credentials, and build/runtime configuration — not the low-risk part of the operator's desk. Editor preferences (`.vscode/`, `.idea/`), prose (everything under `docs/`, plus ROOT-LEVEL `*.md`/`*.rst`/`*.txt` only), root license/notice files, and harmless repository metadata (`.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.editorconfig`, `.dockerignore`) are UNGOVERNED SURFACES (`UNGOVERNED_DIRS`/`UNGOVERNED_ROOT_FILE_RULES` in `scripts/idc_path_gate.py`): they need no authorization and are invisible to an authorization's allowed/denied boundary, in every mode. Agent/CI/container policy (`.claude/`, `.github/`, `.devcontainer/`, `CODEOWNERS`), secret-capable config (`.env*`, `.npmrc`, `.yarnrc*`), dependency/build/container manifests, lockfiles, application tooling config, and `WORKFLOW-config.yaml` (the live enforcement posture) stay gated. Evaluated AFTER the protected-machine check, with `docs/workflow/` subtracted, and with root rules slash-free + case-sensitive, so machine-owned state, the governance anchor, nested application paths, and case variants can never be hand-edited free. A request mixing ungoverned and application paths is judged on the application paths it carries. Pathway posture: mode `off` observes and allows would-be denials; `controlled` and `app-locked` hard-deny. `IDC_HOOKS_OBSERVE_ONLY=1` is a debug-only downgrade that forces observe in any mode. KNOWN NON-COVERAGE of this classifier (F58, extended by F63, narrowed by #192 — pre-existing, tracked as a follow-up, disclosed so the gate is not read as a complete barrier). WHERE THE BOUNDARY RUNS: a protected call is matched when it stands in COMMAND POSITION of a shell segment, or inside a payload/target the gate can follow (`bash|sh|zsh -c`, `bash|sh|zsh FILE`, `source`/`.` FILE, `bash|sh|zsh < FILE`, and — matched as opaque text rather than followed — a scripting interpreter's inline `-c`/`-e` payload, in string form and argv-list form alike); a whole-segment text match runs ONLY as a backstop for a segment that fails to tokenize, and protected words carried as DATA (an argument to some other command) are deliberately not a match. Two F58 channels are CLOSED by #192: the plugin-scripts exemption is now a pinned shipped-scripts manifest, so a non-manifest file dropped into the plugin's scripts/ directory is scanned like any other target; and a scripting-interpreter inline payload (`python3 -c`, `node -e`, …) carrying a protected mutation in string or argv-list form (`subprocess.run(["gh","pr","merge",…])`) is denied. Outside the boundary: PROGRAM TEXT THAT NEVER STANDS IN COMMAND POSITION — an interpreter fed its program on STDIN THROUGH A PIPE (`echo '<protected cmd>' | sh`, `cat payload.sh | bash`, `curl -s <url> | sh`, `echo <base64> | base64 -d | sh`), where the producer segment carries the words as data and the consumer segment is a bare interpreter with no target to follow (the redirection sibling `sh < payload.sh` IS covered), and a protected argv ASSEMBLED BY A HELPER (`echo "pr merge 123" | xargs gh`, where the segment `xargs gh` names no subcommand; `xargs gh pr merge 123` IS covered). THIS LIST IS NOT A CLOSED WORLD: it names what is KNOWN to be uncovered, and a construct absent from it is NOT thereby guaranteed in scope — this is defense-in-depth, not a complete shell parser. An unusable Python runtime is NOT a bypass: the transport hard-denies rather than silently allowing (F57). PostToolUse (Bash): two fail-OPEN, ALWAYS board-coherence self-repair observers (v4 Phase 3 Stage D) — (1) commit-sync: after a successful `git commit`, if the commit's linked board item (derived from the commit message / branch name — no board GraphQL) isn't In Progress, auto-repairs it via `idc_transition.py claim` or injects the exact remediation; (2) issue-create-add: after a successful `gh issue create`, if the same command didn't also add the new issue to the board with Stage+Status, injects the exact remediation. Both never block (additionalContext injection only, never decision:block) and never fire a live board scan. UserPromptExpansion (matched to idc: commands): the command entry gate — before a governed /idc:* command expands, it binds the running plugin runtime to the repo's install receipt (Task-1 freshness) and REFUSES a stale runtime with a /reload-plugins instruction (workflow commands also fail-closed on an invalid/unreadable receipt, naming /idc:doctor + /idc:update; recovery commands may still expand to migrate), and on a current runtime opens the command's lifecycle record + injects the command-contract context. Stop (second handler): the command-closeout gate — a session that entered a governed /idc:* command but never closed it with a valid terminal status (via idc_command_contract.py finish) is refused the stop, bounded N=3 then loud-fail; it self-selects by the session's own open command records and never clears the record itself. The command entry gate runs on IDC command EXPANSION (matched to idc: commands) — deliberately BEFORE governance, so /idc:init in a not-yet-governed repo is still freshness-checked (a stale runtime is refused; a current runtime is admitted with a bootstrap context that opens no record); every OTHER hook here is repo-gated (a no-op outside an IDC-governed repo). All fail-soft; auto-discovered, so NEVER also listed in plugin.json (the 3.1.1 duplicate-hooks regression).
